source_updates.title: Musical Source Separation Bake-Off: Comparing Objective Metrics with Human Perception
findings: the released CSV contains 5889 repeated rating rows from 209 sessions, 50 tracks and four stems
traditional SDR had the highest reported vocal Kendall tau 0.316 in this pool
SI-SAR had the highest reported average among the displayed scale-dependent and invariant panel at tau 0.218
CLAP-LAION-music FAD reached tau 0.253 drums, 0.188 bass and 0.000 vocals
IRM1 oracle masking did not perceptually outperform the strongest learned systems
the Figure 3 and Section 4.2 direction for interference versus artifact weighting contradicts the abstract and conclusion
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Use stem-specific metric panels and blinded listening; keep the interference-versus-artifact weighting claim verification_required until recomputed.

source_updates.title: Spacing Out: On the Reliability of Binaural Music Source Separation Metrics
findings: 26 screened participants contributed 96 pairwise comparisons and 132 localization observations with at least three responses per condition
Bi-SCNet was preferred overall but not significantly for centered sources
delta ILD and SRR aligned more consistently with listener choices than delta ITD and SSR in this experiment
GCC-PHAT delta ITD often collapsed bass estimates to zero microseconds regardless of azimuth
bass ITD failure appeared around 45 dB SNR in the synthetic noise stress test
beta zero improved robustness while beta one better matched clean HRIR ground truth, exposing a robustness-accuracy tradeoff
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Do not use one binaural metric as a production gate; GCC-PHAT delta ITD is especially unreliable for separated narrow-band bass.

source_updates.title: Do Music Source Separation Models Preserve Spatial Information in Binaural Audio?
findings: Binaural-MUSDB mono-averages MUSDB18-HQ stems and convolves one SADIE II subject HRIR at one static azimuth per source
source angles are sampled once per song in 10 degree increments without overlap
the study used objective metrics plus preliminary author listening rather than a controlled perceptual validation
the later 2026 paper directly narrows confidence in the earlier delta ITD conclusions
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Treat this as foundational same-family context, not independent confirmation or a raw rock multitrack reference.

findings: listener CSV is public, 635598 bytes, 5889 rows plus header, 209 sessions, 50 tracks and four stem classes
violation counts reproduce the paper: 2371 zero, 1778 one, 1284 two, 396 three, 60 four
the 1284062239-byte separated-audio archive was not downloaded

knowledge_cards: Separation-metric validity is stem- and failure-mode-specific; a global average can conceal reversals.
Traditional SDR can outperform scale-invariant metrics when gain and spatial fidelity are perceptually relevant.
SI-SAR can better follow instrument-stem judgments but is not a universal production threshold.
CLAP-FAD is distributional and showed modest instrument agreement and zero vocal correlation in this pool.
Internally contradictory metric-weight interpretations remain verification_required.
Repeated ratings require participant- and track-aware uncertainty rather than row-level independence.
An oracle mask is not necessarily a perceptual upper bound.
Binaural metric agreement changes with source position, especially for centered sources.
Full-whitening GCC-PHAT can collapse narrow-band bass ITD under low-energy artifacts.
Reducing PHAT whitening improves robustness but can reduce clean-reference accuracy.
Delta ILD and SRR can track level and residual error without proving localization fidelity.
Single-HRTF static synthetic scenes do not validate measured rooms or ordinary stereo-rock mix controls.
